EX-99.1 2 pmn-ex99d1.htm EX-99.1 Exhibit 99.1 ​ ​ ProMIS Neurosciences Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Reaffirms First Quarter 2027 Topline Data Timing ● PRECISE-AD Phase 1b clinical trial in Alzheimer’s patients remains on track for unblinded 12-month topline data in the first quarter of 2027, including full safety, biomarker and cognitive outcomes data ● PMN310 binds selectively to toxic amyloid-beta oligomers, and its IgG1 backbone is designed to promote clearance of toxic oligomers ● Ivana Rubino, Ph.D., a seasoned Alzheimer’s commercial leader, appointed Chief Commercial Officer ● Cash of $44.1 million as of September 30, 2026, expected to fund operations through 2027, beyond the anticipated PRECISE-AD topline data readout Cambridge, Massachusetts, November 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- ProMIS Neurosciences Inc.

(Nasdaq: PMN), a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on the generation and development of antibody therapeutics targeting toxic misfolded proteins in neurodegenerative diseases, today announced its financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided a corporate update. ​ “The third quarter of 2026 has been productive for ProMIS, following encouraging interim data from our Phase 1b PRECISE-AD trial in Alzheimer’s disease (AD),” said Neil Warma, President and Chief Executive Officer of ProMIS Neurosciences.

If PMN310 is able to shift the benefit-risk profile as compared to the existing standard of care, with ARIA rates similar to placebo and, at a minimum, similar efficacy, we believe PMN310 could be positioned to take a leadership position in the treatment not only of early AD patients, but potentially of asymptomatic (preclinical) AD patients.” ​ “With PRECISE-AD closing out its final stage of patient visits, we look forward to reporting topline data in the first quarter of 2027, which will include safety, biomarker and clinical efficacy measures.

In parallel, we are advancing development of a subcutaneous formulation of PMN310 and preparing for a registrational study that, subject to FDA feedback, we anticipate initiating toward the end of 2027.” Corporate Highlights Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) Program (PMN310) — PRECISE-AD Interim Data and Development Update ● The Company believes that PMN310 has a differentiated design based on (1) selectivity: in preclinical studies, PMN310 bound toxic amyloid-beta oligomers while avoiding monomers, fibrils and plaque; and (2) antibody structure: an IgG1 backbone, as used by lecanemab and donanemab, intended to support Fc receptor–mediated microglial effector function.

Together with the encouraging blinded interim safety observations described below, these features support a distinct clinical hypothesis. ● At AAIC 2026, ProMIS presented the first human evidence of amyloid-beta oligomer target engagement by PMN310 from its Phase 1a study in healthy volunteers, showing a dose-dependent reduction in detectable amyloid-beta oligomers in cerebrospinal fluid after PMN310 administration. ● On July 28, 2026, ProMIS reported encouraging blinded six-month interim safety and biomarker results from PRECISE-AD in 136 patients: no ARIA-E as of the data cutoff in any APOE genotype (including 11% APOE4 homozygotes), ARIA-H of 4.4% (all mild and asymptomatic), no drug-related discontinuations or treatment-related serious adverse events, and a decrease from baseline of approximately 15% in plasma pTau217 and 13.3% in CSF MTBR-tau243 in the pooled, blinded population. ● At topline data, the Company will evaluate the totality of the data for evidence of an improved benefit-risk profile.

Future Activities and Upcoming Milestones ● The PRECISE-AD six-month interim data were selected for poster presentation at the 2026 Clinical Trials in Alzheimer’s Disease (CTAD) conference, taking place November 16–19, 2026, in Boston. ● Abstracts on the PRECISE-AD trial and on the activity of the PMN440 alpha-synuclein vaccine have been selected for platform presentations at the 2027 AD/PD conference. ● Completion of all PRECISE-AD patient visits, expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. ● Presentation of unblinded 12-month topline data from PRECISE-AD, anticipated in the first quarter of 2027.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights ● Cash Position: Cash was $44.1 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $6.1 million as of December 31, 2025, reflecting net proceeds of $70.1 million from the Company’s January 2026 private placement. ● Cash Runway: Based on its current operating plan, the Company expects that its existing cash will be sufficient to fund operating expenses and capital expenditure requirements through 2027, well beyond the anticipated first quarter 2027 PRECISE-AD topline data readout. ● Research and Development (R&D) Expenses: R&D expenses were $6.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $9.8 million for the same period in 2025.

Specifically, this news release contains forward-looking information relating to the Company’s PRECISE-AD Phase 1b clinical trial; the interpretation and clinical significance of the blinded six-month interim safety and biomarker data (including ARIA, pTau217, and MTBR-tau243 findings) described in this release; the expected timing and nature of topline clinical data of PMN310 and the criteria by which the Company will evaluate those results; the anticipated timing and potential outcomes of interactions with the FDA, including a planned meeting in 2027, and the potential benefits of Fast Track Designation; the development of a subcutaneous formulation, its potential benefits, and the Company’s plans to incorporate it into future clinical development; PMN310’s mechanism of action and potential benefits; the potential for PMN310 to offer a differentiated efficacy and safety profile relative to plaque-directed antibodies and other oligomer-directed antibodies; the potential clinical utility and competitive positioning of PMN310, including its potential to achieve a leadership position in the treatment of early AD and its potential use in asymptomatic or preclinical AD, including with respect to comparisons made to existing approved treatments or candidates in development; the Company’s belief that toxic soluble amyloid-beta oligomers are a primary driver of cognitive decline in AD; the advancement, development plans and potential therapeutic benefits of the Company’s preclinical antibody, intrabody and vaccine programs, including PMN267, PMN442, PMN311, PMN440 and PMN260; and the Company’s expectation that existing cash resources will fund planned operations through 2027.
